name: Nova Scotia Archives
description: Nova Scotia's provincial archives, which preserves government and private records and publishes online exhibits such as African Nova Scotians in the Age of Slavery and Abolition.

name: Library and Archives Canada
description: Canada's national library and archives, which publishes research guides and name databases (including the Book of Negroes, 1783) and holds microfilm of many Loyalist-era records.

name: Parks Canada
description: The federal agency that supports the Historic Sites and Monuments Board of Canada and publishes profiles of national historic persons, places and events.

name: The National Archives (UK)
description: The UK government's national archive at Kew. It holds the British copy of the 1783 Book of Negroes in the Carleton papers (PRO 30/55/100).

name: Acadiensis (journal, UNB Libraries)
description: Scholarly journal of Atlantic Canadian history, hosted online by UNB Libraries; back issues also appear on Érudit.

name: The Ontario Historical Society
location: 34 Parkview Ave., Willowdale, Ontario M2N 3Y2, Canada
description: Society that publishes the peer-reviewed journal Ontario History; issues from Autumn 2005 on are open access on Érudit, apart from the latest 12 months.

name: Fernwood Publishing
location: Halifax, Nova Scotia and Winnipeg, Manitoba
description: Independent Canadian publisher of critical scholarly, literary and general-interest books, including the Roseway list.

name: Canadiana (Canadian Research Knowledge Network)
description: Online digital library of Canadian documentary heritage (books, serials, newspapers) run by the Canadian Research Knowledge Network, with scans contributed by partner libraries and archives.

name: Acadia University, Vaughan Memorial Library
description: Acadia University's library, whose copy of the 1885 African Baptist Association minutes was digitized for Canadiana.

name: Halifax Municipal Archives
description: Repository for the historical municipal government records of Halifax, Dartmouth, Bedford and the former County of Halifax, plus community records from the region.

name: MEM - Centre des mémoires montréalaises
description: City of Montréal memory centre whose French-language online encyclopedia (Encyclopédie du MEM) covers Montreal history and communities.

name: Great Unsolved Mysteries in Canadian History (Les grands mystères de l'histoire canadienne)
description: Bilingual educational history project that publishes transcribed primary documents, with archival references, for case studies such as the 1734 Angélique trial.

name: Bibliothèque et Archives nationales du Québec
description: Quebec's national library and archives, holding New France judicial records, including the 1734 Angélique trial file.

name: Toronto Public Library
description: Public library system whose Digital Archive and Baldwin Collection of Canadiana include early Toronto manuscripts and images.

name: Archives of Ontario
description: Provincial archives of Ontario, holding government and private records, including major fonds on Black communities in Ontario (e.g. Alvin D. McCurdy, Mary Ann Shadd Cary).

name: City of Toronto Archives
description: Municipal archives of the City of Toronto. No record in this dataset yet; cited in the holder note for SRC-016.

name: City of Vancouver Archives
description: The City of Vancouver's archives, with civic records and private photograph collections about Vancouver.

name: Canadian Museum for Human Rights
description: National museum about human rights; publishes curator-written stories on Canadian human rights history.

name: Government of Saskatchewan – Heritage Property Search
description: The Saskatchewan government's online documents for designated heritage properties in the province.

name: Fredericton Region Museum
description: Regional history museum in Fredericton that created the online exhibit Our Black Heritage: Early Black Settlers of York-Sunbury Counties (New Brunswick) 1783-Present.

name: Provincial Archives of New Brunswick
location: Bonar Law-Bennett Building, 23 Dineen Drive, University of New Brunswick campus, Fredericton, New Brunswick
description: New Brunswick's provincial archives, which collect, preserve and give access to records of the province's history and people.
